scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: Office A users report their default gateway (10.1.0.1)
"keeps dropping out" for a few seconds at random times, and they suspect the
VRRP first-hop redundancy between the distribution switches is flapping or
that DSW-A1 is failing. They want the flapping gateway fixed. Please confirm
the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: First-hop redundancy (VRRP via keepalived) for VLAN 10 on the Distribution Switches A.

Mechanism: Office A clients use 10.1.0.1 as their default gateway. Today, VRRP is not running, so the virtual IP 10.1.0.1 is statically present on dswa1 only. ARP on clients resolves 10.1.0.1 to dswa1’s bridge MAC (2a:dc:98:19:3f:7e), and dswa2 never owns the VIP. With no active VRRP, there is no timely failover; any brief hiccup on dswa1 looks like the “gateway dropping out,” which users misinterpret as VRRP flapping.

Localization: 
- dswa1: br0.10 has both 10.1.0.2/24 and 10.1.0.1/32 (VIP). keepalived service is inactive (dead). 
- dswa2: br0.10 has 10.1.0.3/24 only; no 10.1.0.1/32 present. keepalived service is inactive (dead).
- Clients (pc1, pc2): ip neigh 10.1.0.1 → lladdr 2a:dc:98:19:3f:7e (dswa1); short test pings to 10.1.0.1 succeed, confirming no current flap but single-homing to dswa1.

Root cause: keepalived (VRRP) is not running on either dswa1 or dswa2, while VIPs were left configured on interfaces, leaving 10.1.0.1 anchored to dswa1 with no redundancy.

Corrective fix: 
- Remove statically configured VIPs (10.1.0.1/32 on dswa1 br0.10 and other VRRP VIPs on both DSWs).
- Start and enable keepalived on dswa1 and dswa2 so VIP ownership is managed by VRRP as per configuration (dswa1 MASTER, dswa2 BACKUP for VI_10).
- Optionally reduce advert_int to 1s (or use VRRP preempt delay) for faster failover.
- Verify clients learn the VIP via GARP and test controlled failover between dswa1 and dswa2.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Fails — the agent reports keepalived inactive and a statically-anchored VIP on DSW-A1 rather than noting DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline.

The agent's conclusions (keepalived inactive on both DSWs, VIP present only on dswa1, clients ARP to dswa1, pings succeed) are supported by the logged outputs; the jump to this explaining the user's intermittent reports is plausible but not proven by observed events. Investigation is thorough and inferences mostly follow from the evidence.
